args: Inspect mrbgems/mruby-binding/src/binding.c, especially binding_proc_new_lvspace and binding_wrap_lvspace. What exact GC invariant is violated, what allocation can trigger GC, and which fix best matches mruby's conventions: moving mrb_add_irep before MRB_OBJ_ALLOC, adding mrb_write_barrier after child stores, or both? Please note any rooting concern for lvspace while mrb_add_irep runs.

The supplied ASan report is a heap-use-after-free in mrb_gc_mark after Binding creation/copy. The stated root cause is that binding_proc_new_lvspace allocates an RProc, then calls potentially allocating mrb_add_irep, and only afterward directly assigns lvspace->upper and lvspace->e.env without a field barrier. The proc is arena rooted but can turn black/old during the intervening GC; then a white/young environment is installed and later swept. I have not yet edited anything. I need a minimal root-cause patch under the project source tree that preserves Binding behavior and follows existing mruby GC/write-barrier patterns.
